utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have appearances for today, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning counsel. Good morning everyone in the courtroom. Mark Harmon, Lorna Bolton, and Carmela Javier for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to all the parties to the proceedings. The Defence of Mr. Perisic is represented by Tina Drolec today, who is for the first time also Case Manager; Chad Mair; our intern Alex Fielding; and Novak Lukic as chief Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Just to place on the record that we are sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis in the absence of Judge David who is not here because of health reasons. May I just also start off by apologising for starting late. It was due to circumstances beyond our control. Before we call the witness, there is an oral decision to be rendered. I think the Defence filed some response last Friday night. We need to deal with the motion related thereto. The Trial Chamber is seized of a Prosecution motion for leave to file a tenth supplemental Rule 65 ter list and request to tender certain exhibits from the bar table filed on the 16th of October, 2009, hereinafter referred to separately as Prosecution 65 ter list motion, and third bar table motion. On the 23rd of October, 2009, the Defence filed a response to the Prosecution 65 ter list motion only with respect to the documents relevant to the evidence of Major General Mungo Melvin. On the 26th of October, 2009, the Trial Chamber pursuant to Rule 127 of the rules, issued an oral decision partly granting the Defence's request for an extension of time in relation to both the second and third bar table motion and stated that the Trial Chamber remained seized of the Prosecution 65 ter list motion with respect to the remaining documents. On the 30th of October 2009, a Defence response to Prosecution motion for leave to file a tenth supplemental Rule 65 ter exhibit list was filed with respect to the remainder of the tenth supplemental Rule 65 ter list. In light of the arguments submitted by the Prosecution, and having considered the arguments advanced by the Defence, the Trial Chamber is satisfied that the Prosecution has shown good cause to amend its consolidated exhibit list at this stage of the proceedings, and has demonstrated the prima facie relevance and probative value of these documents in relation to issues raised in the indictment, as well as to the witness's credibility. The Trial Chamber pursuant to Rules 54 and 65 ter of the rules find that it is in the interest of justice to grant the addition of the remaining items on the 10th supplemental list to the Prosecution's consolidated exhibit list. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, Ms. Bolton will lead the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Bolton. Good morning to you, Madam Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. The next witness for the Prosecution is Ned Krayishnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Will you please make the declaration, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Krayishnik.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Are you receiving any translation through your headphones, or are you just receiving the English?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I may need sometime translation, some words are not that I use every day.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Right now are you getting just English, or are you also getting the B/C/S translation?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: English.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If you need to switch at any point in time, just let us know, okay.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, could you tell us in what country you were born?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I was born in former Yugoslavia, in, presently, Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Whereabouts?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: West east 20 kilometres from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And what is your ethnicity, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: What is my what?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: While you were living in the former Yugoslavia, did you perform any service with the JNA, the army?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: The Yugoslav Army, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I went to the army 1962, until 196 -- 1963 until 1965.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And can you tell the Chamber where you were living, what country you were living in between the years 1992 and 1996.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Canada.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And could you tell the Chamber approximately how old you were when you first moved to Canada?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I was 22.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm just going to ask you, if you can, to remember to pause a little bit after my question before you answer so that it can be translated. Okay.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Sure, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And can you just tell the Chamber very briefly why it was that you left the former Yugoslavia and went to Canada?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Well, it was -- at the time it was a communist system, and I didn't feel any democracy, and my father was monarchist during the Second World War, he was serving in the General Mihajlovic armed forces which was called regular Yugoslavian army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say he was a soldier in Germany or in General Mihajlovic's forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: General Mihajlovic's forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you, I just want to talk to you about your contact with the Office of the Prosecutor, that's the office that I work for. On August 9th of this year, did you have a meeting with myself and a gentleman named Julian Nicholls of the Office of the Prosecutor at a hotel in Canada?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you remember those -- the discussions that we had were recorded in any fashion?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I believe that it was recorded. Actually, it was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to review a transcript of the recording?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And I'm just going to suggest you pointed out a couple of errors in the transcription during that process.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And I'll just identify some of those for the Court. One of them was that there was a gentleman in the transcript who was repeatedly referred to as a Mr. Akanovic. What is that gentleman's actual name?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Rakanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could you just spell that for the Court reporter, please.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: R-a-k-a-n-o-v-i-c.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: There was also a misspelling, as I understand it, of the name of a Bishop or a metropolitan, what is his actual name?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: His name was Bishop Irinej.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: How would you spell that?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I-r-i-n-e-j.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And prior to that first meeting with us on the 9th of August, 2009, had you had the opportunity to review any videotapes, diaries, photographs, or any other materials that would refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Would you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Prior to that first meeting in August 2009 with myself and Mr. Nicholls, had you had the opportunity to review any video-tapes, or photographs, diaries, anything to refresh your memory about the things we discussed?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: There was, I'm going to suggest, a second meeting on the 10th of September, 2009, again with myself and this time with an RCMP officer named John McMath. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And at that time did you provide a statement to Officer McMath and myself?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could I just -- Court's indulgence. Yes, I'm sorry I'm going to pulling up doc ID 1D04-0461.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: In a moment, sir, there should be a document appearing on the screen in front of you. While we are waiting for that document to appear, sir, can you tell the Trial Chamber whether during that second set of meetings in Toronto -- or, sorry, not Toronto -- the second set of meetings in Ontario in September, at that time did you have the opportunity to review any photographs, videotapes, or other materials to refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did those materials assist you in refreshing your memory?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. There should be a document now before you both in English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And if I could ask the court clerk, please, to go to the last page of each document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: In the English document, sir, you should see a signature. Can you tell me whose signature that is?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: It is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And you'll see in paragraph 31, for example, there's a word that's been crossed out Kolevic, and written above it is a different spelling of that word. Could you tell me who -- at whose request that correction was made.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And did you have an opportunity to review the statement then and make corrections before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And having had your memory refreshed as a result of the materials you reviewed, did you make some corrections in that second statement to the original audio-taped statement you'd given?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm done with that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I want to take you back, sir, to the time-period 1992 to 1996. Are you familiar with an organisation called the - it was a Canadian organisation - called the Serbian Republic Humanitarian Organisation?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What kind of an organisation was that?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: It was a humanitarian organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately what year it was established or founded?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I'm not sure exactly, but I think it was established in 1992 sometime.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Who were the founders?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: It was registered, I believe, in Hamilton by Mr. Lesic and Jovan Grubor, Ranko Rakanovic, and myself. And there were some other people that I forgot their name now.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: When we are talking about Hamilton, we are talking about Hamilton, Ontario?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, Hamilton, Ontario, Canada.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And the other gentlemen that you named, Mr. Lesic, Mr. Gruber, Mr. -- is it Jokanovic?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: No, Rakanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: It's Rakanovic; it's the same person that -- whose name you corrected the spelling of earlier?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Were these individuals you knew before the institution was founded, or are these people you met in the course of founding the organisation?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I knew those three individuals before.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And what was it that prompted you to establish this organisation?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Well, we were watching the news and the war started in Bosnia or former Yugoslavia, and I saw on the TV, saw my own distant relative, that they were locked in a house and burned in the house. And then I was watching the news, and I saw that there were the people, saw my own relatives were displaced all over the place, that nobody knew where they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So what did you set out to do then by founding this institution?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Well, we thought that we should be able to get together and try to find those people and assist them in -- in the necessity, whatever, either clothing or food or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Was the organisation involved in any fundraising in Canada for those purposes?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And who were the intended recipients of the fundraising or the aid that you intended or hoped to deliver?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Well, we tried to find it through the government and through the army. The government told us that they wouldn't know where they had -- that the army would be able to assist us and find where the people might be and where can we locate them and help them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Let me ask the question in a different way. Was your intention to provide aid to people in what region, first of all?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Well, there was not really a region. We thought that wherever it was necessary, wherever the people were located or placed or whatever. Or hospital or camps or whatever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just get some clarity, sir. Was this aid intended for your relatives and distant relatives, or was it intended for everybody in former Yugoslavia that you thought was a victim in the manner that you described people locked up in houses and displaced?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in general to help anybody that was in a need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Was the aid that you delivered provided to people of all ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I don't think so because we wouldn't be able to reach any other ethnicities and which was controlled with the other ethnic territories.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that your group did some fundraising. Were they successful in actually raising some money or other tangible goods for delivery to the region?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: It was fairly, not huge quantity, but it was -- we were able to raise the funds from the people that -- because everybody more or less had somebody that was affected.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And how would you go about ensuring that the funds reached the people in need? Would you just wire the money over?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Well, we couldn't wire it. We usually took it over with us. We always had -- our treasurer was always going because he was in charge of it, and somebody would most of the time accompany him. And then when we arrived we would find out where was most needed and how to be located.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Who was the treasurer?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Lesic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What is his first name?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Milan.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did you personally make any trips to the region between 1992 and 1996?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could you approximate how many trips you made.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Approximately I think I made about five, six trips. I'm not exactly sure, but in that vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. I don't intend to ask you about all your trips, sir, but I do want to ask you about the first trip you made. Can you recall what year and what month you made that first trip to the region on behalf of the humanitarian organisation?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: It was in December 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did anybody accompany you?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: From Canada was Mr. Lesic and myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And I am assuming you flew out of Canada, you didn't take a boat?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes. We flew.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Where did you -- what country did you fly into?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: We flew to, I believe, Budapest and Hungary, and from Budapest we drove, we came by taxi.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: By taxi to where?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: To Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: During this trip, what was the -- what was the nature of the aid you were intending to deliver?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: It was money because this was our first trip, and we thought the only thing they could buy what needed to be bought over there, and we had no way of taking it any other way over there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And prior to that first trip, had you any contacts in the region or made any prior arrangements for who was going to get the money?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So when you arrive in Belgrade then with the money, what do you do?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Then we made some contact and the people, and stayed in Belgrade, I think, for a couple of days until we found a better place called Srpska Vila in Belgrade. And then I run into Bishop Irinej who I knew from before through the church organisation and diocese.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Who was Bishop Irinej?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: He was the Bishop Metropolitan Irinej for United States and Canada, of Serbian Orthodox diocese.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And so you ran into him in the Srpska Vila in Belgrade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And when you ran into him, did you discuss with him what you were doing there?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I did. He was asking me what I'm doing, and I was asking him what he is doing. And he said, Well, it looks like we are on the same mission.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Was he able to assist you then in finding a place or somebody to give the funds to?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, he was. He had a contact with the Metropolitan Nikolas in the Republika Srpska, called Sokolac -- Pale, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. I want to show you another document, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 2085.01, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Again, sir, it should show up on the screen in front of you and in both English and Cyrillic, B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Sorry, what was the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I haven't asked you a question, yet, sir, but thank you for being so attentive.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: In the English version, I'm interested in going to page 76, please. And if we could scroll down the page. I have to apologise to my friends across the courtroom. I can sometimes locate things in B/C/S when it's not written in Cyrillic, but I really could not figure out what the corresponding page number was in the Cyrillic document. So I hope that doesn't pose my friends any problem. Mr. Lukic, do you need some time, or?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not a problem for me, but I would like for the benefit of my client the Cyrillic version to be displayed. Maybe the legal officer can help us, or the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Or maybe, you, Mr. Lukic, if you have identified the page, you can tell us what page it is so that your client can get to the page too. Now, it's page 17 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: It's 76 to 78 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have -- if I had the document in hard copy before me, it would be easier, but all I have is what I see on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Am I right to say what we have in the B/C/S now on the screen is the first page of the document? Maybe if we can go in that document, deep into the document around 76, 77.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's page 70.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Page 70 we are told it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir -- if we could scroll down, please, on the English page. There's an indication in this document. We saw on the first page that this was a transcript of the proceedings of the 23rd session of the National Assembly of the Republika Srpska held on 17th December, 1992. And about two-thirds down this page there's an indication that we have some guests, Serbs from Canada, Mr. Lesic and Mr. -- it says Kraisnik.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Kraisnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: It's spelled differently. Do you know which Mr. Kraisnik that is?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Kraisnik? Are you talking about me, or are you talking --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Well, were you at the Serb assembly on the 17th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And if we could move forward in that document, please, to the next page, page 77 in English. I'm sure it will be on the next page in B/C/S as well.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I'm getting a little bit confused. What is the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, that's -- we use that term to refer to Bosnian Serbian Croatian. So when --

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Can we refer to Serbian?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I can try to refer to Serbian.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: It's a bad habit.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Certainly. You'll see on the English version, sir, on page 77. If we could scroll up a little bit, there's some text that starts with the name Ned Krayishnik. And scrolling down again on the page, we have a second paragraph that indicates -- starts with saying: "We decided to come here to help as much as we can. Mr. Milan Lesic delivered $15.000 here for the media and propaganda, for I think that we have lost the war the most in that area, and our enemies have been the most successful on that account. In addition, Lesic also decided to make a contribution to the Ministry of Defence and our government, and since you know best where it is most needed, you will solve that the best. He is again given $10.000 personally. Mr. Slobodan Nikolic, an industrious Serb from Jelinek near Belgrade, owns a small machine shop. Somebody knocks on his door every day, and he never says that cannot contribute. He contributes every day, and if it is twice a day, again he gives. We've also brought $10.000 he sent. I, too, am giving $10.000 may name, the $15 .000 given by my brother Lesic..." And then they go on to explain some more. Do you recognise that, sir, as being a portion of the speech that you made to the assembly on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And if my math is correct, the total amount of aid then given was about $45.000?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Probably, yeah. I didn't add it, but, yeah, it would be.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Could you just explain, then. You told us that --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I just want pages 76 to 78 of this document marked as an exhibit. That's the portion that we've been dealing with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And page 1, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Am I right to say this is ID 040461?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: No, this is 65 ter 2085.01.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What happened to 040461?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I was not seeking to tender it in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. [Microphone not activated] 65 ter 0885 -- 2085.1 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. I'm so sorry. Many things going wrong this morning. 65 ter 2085.01 admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number and marked for identification. What did you say, ma'am? Did you say MFI?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: No, I did not. I often do, but not today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Not today. Thank you. Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 02085.01, pages 1, 76, and 77 in English; pages 70, 71, and first page in B/C/S shall be Exhibit P2789. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The Chamber will just need a little bit of an explanation, sir, how it came to pass that you were in Belgrade where you ran into the metropolitan, and then ultimately you were in the Serb -- Bosnian Serb Assembly. First of all, where was that Bosnian Serb Assembly meeting that we were referring to?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Pale.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So could you just explain how you came to be connected into Pale?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Well, we flew by helicopter, Red Cross helicopter. And when we arrived there, then it happened that they had assembly same time, and we were told that we should go to the assembly and give our donation and metropolitan arranged that we get there and address the assembly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So would I be fair in saying that the metropolitan was the one who was able to help you make the contact and so forth?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Prior to December 1992, had you ever met any high-ranking politician in the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And how about any high-ranking military official in the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: As a result of your attendance at the assembly, did you have the opportunity in December 1992 to meet some military and political officials?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I just have a couple of photographs I'd like to show you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And the first is 65 ter 9600.02.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you asking me, or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, again, the photograph is going to magically appear on the screen in front of you in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Can that be made a little bigger. Great.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Where was this photograph taken?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I believe this was done in Pale.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And what month and year?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: In December 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Going from left to right in the photo, can you help us by identifying the people.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: General Ratko Mladic, President Radovan Karadzic, Mr. Milan Lesic, General Milan Gvero, and myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. You are the individual with the moustache at the time?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If that could be marked as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's marked as an exhibit. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document becomes Exhibit P2790. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And if I could have 65 ter 9600.03, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: When, relative to the last photo, was this photograph taken?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: This one?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I believe this was also in Pale.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And in terms of the date?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I believe it was evening, night.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, evening of what day?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I believe it was 17th.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Of?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: December 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And again just going from first the back row, left to right.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Myself; General Gvero, Milan; and General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Front row?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Front row, Bishop Irinej. And the gentleman next to him, I don't recall his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And when was this get-together relative to the assembly meeting that you attended?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I believe this was after the assembly meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If that could be marked as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is so marked. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this document becomes Exhibit P2791. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You've told us that on that first trip you were in Belgrade and then you visited Pale. Do you recall if you travelled anywhere else in the Republika Srpska on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, we did. From Pale we went to Kasindol. And on the way we stopped on one place, which was right down the main road to Kasindol. I think it's called Trebinje, I'm not sure. I'm sorry, not Trebinje. The -- I cannot recall the name now, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: It's all right, sir. Approximately how long did you stay for that -- during that first trip? How long were you in the region?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I believe we were there altogether two or three days. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Two or three days in Bosnia, or two or three days in Bosnia and Serbia?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: In Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. When you -- I take it you returned to Canada after this trip?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: When you returned to Canada, did either yourself or Mr. Lesic maintain any contact with any of the people you had met during that first trip in December 1992?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: We might have, but I don't remember, maybe later on. I don't know how late or what time. I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. You've told us that you've made subsequent trips. During any of your subsequent trips, did you have the opportunity to meet any of the family members of any high-ranking military officials, first?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: My family members in the military?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: No, their family members.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: My first trip I don't -- no, I didn't meet any family members of the --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Later on?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Later on I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Whose family members did you meet?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I met General Mladic wife and daughter, and also I met President Karadzic wife.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And were you ever invited to the homes of any politicians in the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I was invited to Momcilo Krajisnik once for a very brief, maybe less than an hour. We had a coffee, and it was not too far away from the -- it was in Pale. But I met his, I believe it was three or four children that he had.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Apart from the contact -- sorry, let me just show you a couple of other photos, sir. You've told us you made subsequent trips.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 9600.10, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Showing you a photo, sir, and it has -- appears to be a date stamp on the lower right corner 93/10/9. First of all, do you recognise this photo?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Are you visible in this photo?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Where are you?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I'm at the left far end.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Where was this photo taken?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: In Han Pijesak, Crna Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Han Pijesak, Crna Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Where is Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Han Pijesak is -- I'm not sure. Approximately around 40 kilometres from Pale.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And is it --

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: East.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry. Is it part of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What was at Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: It was the headquarters of Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: When you say the Serbian army, are you talking about the Bosnian Serbian army, or the --

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I'm talking about the Bosnian Republika Srpska army.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And you also referred to it as Crna -- I get this wrong.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Crna Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Exactly, Crna Rijeka. Is there any difference between Han Pijesak and Crna Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: It's the same vicinity, maybe just outskirt of the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And can you just assist us, please, in -- first of all, is the date stamp correct of 93/10/9?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I don't see the date on it this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: On the lower right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Oh, yeah. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And can you assist us going around the table from front left as to who is there.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Milan Lesic, General Milan Gvero, and Mrs. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So you've obviously skipped yourself.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And on the other side of the table then, there's only one woman there, that's Mrs. Mladic?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Next to her?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I believe the -- it's a very not clear picture. I think General Mladic, but I cannot see it very clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: And then next to him is Marko Sandalj and General Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: General Dragomir Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And the man you indicated was next to Mr. General Milosevic is from where?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Canada.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And how do you spell his last name?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: S-a-n-d-a-l-j.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And is he part of the humanitarian work that you were doing?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Brief indulgence. If that could be marked as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So marked. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This becomes Exhibit P2792. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And if I could have 65 ter 9600.11, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: All right. There's a couple of people in this photo that don't appear to have been in the one we just dealt with. This is also dated 93/10/9. Is this the same or a different location as the last photo we discussed?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Same location.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The gentleman to the far right of the photo at the very front, do you recognise him or remember his name?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: At the head table?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: At the far right of the photo, the person -- you can see the badge on his uniform.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: No, that's the head of the table. I'm talking about far right of the photo, the person who has got the date stamp over top of them.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I don't know his name. He was there, but I never met him after or before.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recognise persons who are seated next to General Dragomir Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are going to confuse us, Madam Bolton. If you start with this gentleman, why don't you go around the table.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: We'll go around the table, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Let's start with the gentleman on the far left of the photo, sir. With the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: On the far left of the photo. You started on the far right the photo. Now where are you going?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I was going to go left to right, Your Honour, as opposed to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. If you go left to right, now you are starting with the man with the mustache, which I suspect is the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The gentleman on the far left in the army uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, the gentleman right at the beginning of the table. The man sitting opposite the man with the date stamp.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, that's who we are going to start with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did you understand, Mr. Krayishnik, that I'd like to start with the gentleman on the far left of the photo with the mustache in the uniform, and could we go around the table from him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I want to be sure we are on the same page. When you say far left, I'm talking approximate of the person near left, the very first person on the left.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm talking -- that's the same person we are talking about, Your Honour. I'm saying only saying far, because he is the farthest left in the photo, I guess. But he is the closest person in the photo.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So to make a simple matter very complicated, as I like to do, if we could start with that gentleman and go around the table, please, Mr. Krayishnik.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: We are starting from my left and going around?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: It's General Dragomir Milosevic, and next to him I don't see the face.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I can't remember who was it. And then next looks like it's a woman; I don't know her either. And then next one is General Ratko Mladic wife and General Mladic. And General Milan Gvero. And I'm not sure, it looks like there is somebody between General Gvero and Mr. Lesic, but I don't see the -- then I see Milan Lesic, and then myself, and Marko Sandalj.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And you've already identified the other gentleman.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Which other gentleman?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, the person next to Mr. Sandalj, closest to the camera.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yeah, that is myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: No, the person on the other side of Mr. Sandalj.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Milan Lesic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: No, the --

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Oh, the first person.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't recognise that person.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Excuse me --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You were talking about the person with the numbers on his shoulder. Is that what you're asking?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yeah. I don't know that gentleman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Excuse me asking this question. The person that you point as yourself doesn't seem to have a moustache this time; am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's right, the second person on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Third person on the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Third person. Okay, so we can't see your face. We can't whether you do or do not have. Okay. Now, you are the third person. The second person on the right, who is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Marko Sandalj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. And the person on the other side of you, that's the person that you don't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The person to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The person on your right, on the right of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On my right with the numbers on the shoulder, I don't know him, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry. I think we've confused things. If you were seated at the table, sir, the person who was on your right with the striped shirt and the jacket and the dark hair slicked back?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: That's Milan Lesic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If I could have that marked as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is marked. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This document becomes Exhibit P2793.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Other than having contact with some military officials and politicians from the Republika Srpska in the region, between 1992 and 1996 did you have any contact with any politicians or military people outside of the Balkans?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I did one time in New York.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If I could just show you -- sorry, did you want to take a break, Your Honour? I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed. I realise -- it looks like we've gone far beyond it, in fact. If we could -- what time do we normally take our break? We would have taken it at quarter past to quarter to. Okay. Let's take it to 11.00.00 and come back. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you proceed, Madam Bolton, just if the record could just show that the Chamber has been advised that for the first 12 minutes of this morning's session we were not broadcast. It was not because we were in private session, it is simply because there was a technical hitch. And I don't think the public missed much because what was happening then was just introductory remarks about the witness. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, you told us that you made several trips on behalf of your humanitarian organisation to deliver, amongst other things, money to organisations in the Republika Srpska. Can you tell me if you had any mechanism for proving to the people who donated the money in Canada that in fact you had done what you said you would do and delivered it to the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes. It was video-taped camera, mostly Mr. Lesic had. And when they were delivery, whatever it was, it was a video camera, and we showed -- when we returned back home we would show to our board directors and sometime to public when we were fundraising again.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So did Mr. -- how much videotape did Mr. Lesic generate sort of typically in a trip?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I don't know. I never kept a record of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Is Mr. Lesic camera shy?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And other than -- we've seen some photographs here as well, how often were photographs taken?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I presume whenever it was necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Were you doing any videotaping or taking any photographs yourself, or was it others in your group?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I never took any photographs at all. Because I wasn't able to handle the camera physically.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And that's because, as I understand, you had loss of a hand earlier in life; is that fair?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, true.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If I can take your mind now, sir, to July 1995. Could you tell me if you travelled to the Republika Srpska or Serbia in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: When you say "we did," can you tell me who all was on that trip?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Well, on trip with me was Mrs. Ksenija Zarubin and Mr. Branko Zarubin, and Mr. Milan Lesic, and myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You said trip with you, were there others that didn't travel with you?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yeah, there was Mr. Rakanovic brothers, Ranko and Ilija.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Can you just spell, you've already spelled for us, I think Ranko. Ilija, can you spell that for us?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I-l-i-j-a.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And what association, if any, did Mr. and Mrs. Zarubin and the two Rakanovic brothers have to the humanitarian organisation we've been talking about?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Zarubin, fairly wealthy guy, and they were donating money, and we delivered a scanner to VMA. It was in the name of Mrs. Zarubin, she was a nurse in her profession.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. You are giving us quite a bit of information; I'm going to come back to that in a moment. I just have a couple of questions. First of all, these people who were accompanying you, where did these people, not currently reside, but at the time what country were they residing?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Canada.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And in terms of the ethnicity of these people that you've mentioned, what would their ethnicity be?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And what was the -- you've mentioned here something about a scanner being delivered to the VMA. First of all, what is the VMA?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: It was army hospital in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And was it the full scanner that you were delivering?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And when we are talking about a scanner, we are talking about some kind of, I take it, medical device?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: How did you know that the VMA needed a scanner?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: General Mladic faxed to Mr. Lesic the number of the item and when we -- when he got it, he called me and told me what he had, and then we were looking to buy it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection of approximately how much this part cost?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I believe we paid something around $46.000.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: That's Canadian dollars?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And how did you -- sorry, you purchased it then in Canada?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, in Mississauga.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. I'm not going to make you spell Mississauga for the record. I'll tell the reporter later how it's spelled. Did -- I take it from your initial answer about how you were travelling, did you travel in two groups then, two separate groups of people?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Four of us that I mentioned travelled together. Mr. and Mrs. Zarubin and Mr. Lesic and myself. We travelled together to Bulgaria, Sofia; and Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So Bulgaria and then on to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Why was it that you went into Bulgaria first?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: That was the only flight that was available that we can fly closer to Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall the approximate date that you flew over?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Approximate, yeah, probably around 15th or 14th, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And the Rakanovics, at what point did you meet up with them?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: We met them in Belgrade, I think was 16th.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to show you a photograph, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Haven't we already seen that?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I may have the wrong 65 ter number. If I may just have a moment, please. Sorry, I'm dyslexic, I think. 9600.20.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: This photograph, sir, if you look in the bottom right-hand corner has a date 16/7/95. Is that a correct date stamp?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: You said bottom right corner. Oh, okay, I see it. Yeah. 16/7/95, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Best of your recollection, is that date correct?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Looking at the -- going again from left to right in the photograph, first there is a gentleman in a blue suit on the far left of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Who is that?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Ranko Rakanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that a gentleman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that a gentleman, the person in the blue suit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The person standing next to him with a striped shirt whose face we can't see, are you able to say who that is?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. The person who is removing their coat and wearing a white shirt, who is that?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I don't see his clear face, but I think it's Mr. Lesic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The gentleman seated on the couch next to Mr. -- where Mr. Lesic is standing?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Branko Zarubin.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And the woman seated next to him?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Is Mrs. Zarubin.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And the gentleman closest --

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: But I don't see her face. It looks like somebody holding a hand. And I don't see her face. I only see --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I have a print copies of these photos, sir. If at any point you need to see a better version of them, just let me know.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I'm just saying that I am assuming that this is Mrs. Zarubin because, like I say, I don't see her face.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And the person that you think is then closest to us in the photo next to Mrs. Zarubin?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I cannot identify that person. I don't know who it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: With the Court's permission perhaps I could show the witness an actual print copy of the photograph which is much clearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may do so, ma'am, after your opposite number has had a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, if you could just leave the photograph with the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Just for the record then, the person you couldn't identify, the gentleman --

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yeah, now I see the picture. This is Mrs. Zarubin.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. It's Mrs. Zarubin and you?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember where this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: In Belgrade. I believe it was in Hyatt Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Is that the full name of the hotel?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Can you see what the object is on the table in front of Mrs. Zarubin? Can you identify that?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I assume a camera. Looks like a camera.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If that photograph, please, could be marked as the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is so marked. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document becomes Exhibit P2794. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You told us that the intended destination for the scanner was an army hospital, the VMA, in Belgrade. Which army was this hospital associated with?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Well, that was Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And you've also told us that -- sorry, I don't think I've asked this before. Your organisation, was anyone in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia by which I mean Serbia or Montenegro, were they eligible to receive aid from your organisation?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I don't think so, but the Serbian army from Republika Srpska, most of them, they were treated at the VMI -- VMA.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: All right. Sir, I'm going to start by showing you some video footage. And we'll be stopping and starting at different points, and then I'll be asking you some questions, okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: It's for the record -- sorry, Court's indulgence. The 65 ter number is 9597. And I'll indicate to assist the Court as well that there is a full transcription of the audio available in B/C/S and English at 65 ter 9597.01, but there are also subtitles that will follow the video as it plays. Okay. Hopefully that was clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But for what -- for purposes of this clip you are going to play, the 65 ter is 9597, without a point number?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. If we could start the tape at the 1 minute mark, and then we'll be stopping it at 1 minute and 6 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Switch off your microphone if you want to whisper to your --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. That's a very short clip. Did you recognise the location of that clip at all?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Could you back the picture, please, because I only see now a couple of feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Somebody's --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back to about -- first, about the 1.02 second mark. 1.01. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: We are now at 1.01.08 seconds. Do you recognise that location?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: It looks like it's in Belgrade in the hotel, but I'm not sure. I cannot be precise on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you recognise -- we were looking before at a photo and there was somebody with a striped shirt we couldn't identify. Do you recognise the person with the striped shirt in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I seen him, but I don't know his name, or I don't know who he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And how about the gentleman he is speaking with?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I believe this is Mr. Zarubin, Branko Zarubin.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If we could just fast forward a couple of seconds to 1.03, let's try. 1.04.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you recognise the person on the phone?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I don't. I can't see his face.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: That's fine. We are going to restart the footage, sir. And this next segment is longer. I'm going to play through the segment once, and then we'll backtrack, and I'll ask you to make some identification. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So this next segment is starting at approximately 1 minute and 7 seconds, and it's going until -- I believe it's about 13 minutes and 18 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: First of all, sir, were you present at the meeting that's captured on the footage we just played?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm going to ask for assistance to go back and identify some people. If we could go to the 1 minute and 12 second -- well, actually, where we've stopped the video right now, 13 minutes 18.7 seconds, who is the gentleman drinking out of the cup?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If we could go, please, to the 1 minute and 57 second mark, please. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The gentleman on the far left at the 1.57 mark with the glasses and the mustache, who is that?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: That was me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The gentleman seated next to with you the white shirt and the tie?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Ilija Rakanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The woman in the flowered, either, dress or blouse?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Mrs. Ksenija Zarubin.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And do you recognise this person on the far right of the photo?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. If we could advance to 3 minutes and 46 seconds, please. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The gentleman who has the suit on, on the far left of the photo looking at General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Milan Lesic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you know the woman on the far side of General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I don't have a clear picture, but it looks like, what I see, Mrs. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could we just advance a couple of seconds, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Does that help you at all, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: A little bit, but I think that's Mrs. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: How about the gentleman in the white uniform?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you know what his position was?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I think he was a doctor from ...

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If we could advance to the 6 minute and 9 second mark, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I just want to replay a little section of the tape because in the transcript the speaker isn't identified, and I'm hoping you can help me identify who is speaking.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So if we could play from 6.09 to 6.28.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: We played to the 6.30 mark on the tape. The person who is speaking at that juncture is who?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Ranko Rakanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And if we could advance to the 12 minute and 6 second mark, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you recognise this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I seen him, but I don't remember his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. You told us that you were present at this meeting. Can you tell us if the footage accurately or does not accurately reflect what happened in that meeting.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I believe this was after we made the delivery of the scanner.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, is the footage an accurate representation of what happened at that meeting, or has it been changed in some way?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, does the footage correspond with your memory of what happened with that meeting, or is it different in some way?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: No, it's just, like I said, we were in the hospital in the -- I believe it's a boardroom or something that looks like it. I'm not certain of it. Can you go back maybe that I can see the room a little more clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. We are just advancing backwards slowly. Can you recognise that room?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yeah, I think this was in -- at the hospital in VMA.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: VMA is VMA in English?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: VMA, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: When General Mladic was speaking, he referred to a tube and a lamp.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What was he talking about?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: He was talking about that scanner.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So the scanner that you brought --

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: The tube, yeah. The scanner tube, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The scanner tube is what you brought?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: He also made reference to making some arrangements for cars to come to something he referred to as the Intercontinental. What is the Intercontinental?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I believe it's a hotel in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Is that the same or a different hotel than where you were staying?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: It could be the same. I could have been mistakenly thought it was Hyatt, maybe it was the intercontinental hotel.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Have you had occasion to over the years to stay at both?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately what time of day this meeting in the VMA boardroom was taking place?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I believe it was late afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You said earlier that you thought you arrived on either the 14th or the 15th of July, 1995. Did you have any contact with General Mladic to the best of your recollection on either the 14th or the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And prior to this meeting in the boardroom on the 16th of July, had you had any contact with him?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did General Mladic or anybody else explain what General Mladic was doing in Belgrade that day?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: No, I don't recall that -- did any explanation or reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did he or anyone else indicate how he had spent the first part of the day up until the late afternoon?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Just a couple of questions about some of the things that were said in that segment. One of the suggestions that General Mladic made --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And to assist my friends, this appears in the English transcript at page 2, lines 31 and following.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Was he made a suggestion that -- I want to quote it correctly. He said: "With all these people who participated in this, you should make a list and then you will come to my place and then I will give you a letter of appreciation, and we will list all the people who took part in this process of acquiring this particular spare part. They will have my signature which proves that this has been delivered here. It's all on the camera. Do we understand each other?" First of all, what did you understand him to mean when he was talking about my place?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: That I wasn't sure. But I think we met after that at Crna Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And did you, in fact, follow up and go to Crna Rijeka for that purpose?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, we stopped in Crna Rijeka and when we -- and we went to Pale from Crna Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Rakanovic, when he was making his speech, he made a reference -- and this is at page 4, lines 20 to 24 of the transcript. He says: "I don't want to bother you now with the stories how we came here. We purchased what you wanted us to. I hope -- no, I don't hope, I'm sure we are going to the same in future as well, if necessary. I'd -- I would just like to tell you that the members of the Humanitarian Organisation of Republika Srpska send their regards, wishing you all good and safe journey to Gorazde, should it be." Could you tell me what conversation there had been up to that point in time about anyone going to Gorazde?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Rakanovic, he is from Gorazde, and his brother, I think, and they had family just before Gorazde, a little town, I forgot the name of it. I think he was referring to that, that they were going to Gorazde himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So you think he was addressing himself when wishing himself a good and safe journey to Gorazde?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Well, he was -- yeah, that I think he was referring that would be safe passage or that they can get there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: His actual words are "wishing you all." And I'm just wondering who the "you" is.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: You mean Mr. Rakanovic says?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Rakanovic says: "Wishing you all and safe journey to Gorazde, should it be."

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: I really don't remember paying that attention that he was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And going back to my original question, had there been any discussion of anyone going to Gorazde other than Mr. Rakanovic up to that point in time, that you remember?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: General Mladic indicated -- again this is at page 3 of the transcript at lines, first 6 and 7, he said: "And now you can -- I'm going to see what the Serbs have been doing at Zepa." And then further down the page at lines 21 to 30 he addresses himself to the doctor and makes the suggestion that these people, it says: "Doctor, I'd like to say one more thing afterwards while you were waiting. I'd like to ask you people since you are -- they saved a lot of our people, they have been procuring medicine, prosthesis, they have provided assistance to hospital, they have accommodated wounded people, both Milan Lesic and Mr. Zagarac's son," Milan Lesic interrupts and says "Dejan Zagarac" --

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Dejan Zarubin.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Zarubin. Okay, so the transcript should be Zarubin. Okay.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Zarubin.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: General Mladic continues by saying: "Our wounded men, to talk with them here, maybe some of them have relatives here. After all, we all have relatives here." What I understood is that General Mladic was suggesting that you could visit some of the wounded men; is that fair?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And did you in fact do that?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If we could return to the tape to the 13 minute and 18 second mark. We have a short second that lasts until approximately 15 minutes and 53 seconds that I am going to play for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The gentleman who was speaking on the phone in the last footage we just watched, who is that?
